title: Nvidia Tops WSJ's Inaugural Best Companies for the Future Ranking
summary: Nvidia received the top spot in WSJ's inaugural Best Companies for the Future ranking, which evaluates companies on their capacity for future growth through R&D investment, talent development, and business model diversification. The ranking highlights Nvidia's dominant market position across AI infrastructure hardware and its ability to expand its platform across data center, cloud, and edge computing markets. WSJ described the list as a forward-looking assessment of competitive durability rather than historical financial performance.

title: Top White House AI Advisor to Leave Post
summary: Sriram Krishnan, the top White House artificial intelligence policy advisor, is departing his post, according to The Information. Krishnan had served as the administration's senior AI policy advisor and was a central figure in shaping the White House's approach to AI governance and industry engagement. His departure comes as the administration continues negotiations with major AI developers over financial and regulatory frameworks.

title: Trump Targets Meeting With AI Companies to Discuss Financial Partnerships
summary: The Trump administration is planning a meeting with leading AI companies to explore potential financial partnerships between the government and the private sector. The discussions reflect a broader pattern of the administration seeking equity stakes or revenue-sharing arrangements as part of its approach to AI development, moving beyond traditional procurement frameworks.

title: Goldman, JPMorgan Explore New Ways to Tame AI Lending Risks
summary: Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase are developing new methodologies to assess and manage the credit and operational risks introduced by AI-driven lending decisions, as both banks grapple with growing exposure to AI-generated credit recommendations and automated underwriting systems. The banks are evaluating approaches to stress-test AI lending models for bias, data drift, and systemic concentration risks that differ from those in traditional credit models.

title: Google and Nvidia Consider Intel as Backup Chip Manufacturer
summary: Google and Nvidia are exploring Intel as a potential backup chip manufacturer to reduce strategic dependence on TSMC, according to The Information. The move comes amid continued geopolitical risk around Taiwan-based semiconductor production, and would give both companies contingency options for manufacturing AI accelerators outside TSMC's foundries.

title: Nvidia, SK Hynix Sign Multi-Year Deal for Next-gen AI Memory
summary: Nvidia and SK Hynix have signed a multi-year supply agreement for next-generation high-bandwidth memory products, securing Nvidia's access to HBM4 components critical for its upcoming GPU roadmap. The deal reinforces the two companies' existing supply relationship and positions SK Hynix as a primary memory partner for Nvidia's next wave of AI accelerator products.

title: Reid Hoffman to Depart Microsoft Board
summary: LinkedIn co-founder and venture capitalist Reid Hoffman is departing Microsoft's board of directors, where he has served since Microsoft's 2016 acquisition of LinkedIn. His departure comes as Microsoft continues to restructure its AI and cloud governance and follows a period of increased scrutiny of board composition at major technology companies.

title: Exclusive: Tesla Pushes Roadster Demo to August
summary: Tesla has pushed its next public demonstration of the long-delayed Roadster electric sports car to August, extending a timeline that has seen the vehicle miss multiple target dates since its 2017 debut. The delay continues a pattern of Tesla deprioritizing its premium sports car program in favor of mass-market vehicles and energy products.

title: For a Select Few, IPOs Are Winners. Good Luck to Everyone Else.
summary: WSJ's Heard on the Street column examines the bifurcated IPO market of 2026, in which investors who received shares at the offer price have seen the largest returns while those buying in the aftermarket have largely been disappointed. The piece uses the anticipated SpaceX IPO as an illustration of how access inequality is a structural feature of major listings rather than an anomaly.

title: Democrats Unveil Flood of AI Proposals in Potential Challenge to Tech Giants
summary: Congressional Democrats unveiled a broad package of AI legislative proposals targeting military AI use, algorithmic accountability, and worker protections from AI-driven displacement, representing the most coordinated Democratic push on AI regulation to date. The legislation would impose new transparency and human-oversight requirements on Defense Department AI deployments and establish restrictions on automated weapons systems, previewing the regulatory agenda a future Democratic-led Congress could pursue.

title: The 24-Year-Old AI Wiz Who Counts Jane Street as an Investor
summary: WSJ profiles Leopold Aschenbrenner, a 24-year-old AI fund manager whose firm has attracted Jane Street — one of the most selective allocators in quantitative finance — as an investor and amassed substantial assets under management. The profile examines how Aschenbrenner's background, including a stint at OpenAI, has shaped his concentrated investment thesis on AI infrastructure.

title: Bouygues, Orange, Free Agree €20B SFR Carve-Up
summary: A consortium led by Bouygues Telecom, alongside Orange and Free-Iliad, signed a memorandum of understanding with Altice France to acquire the majority of SFR's assets in a deal valued at approximately €20.35 billion, consolidating France's mobile market from four to three major operators. Bouygues will take a 42% stake, Free-Iliad 31%, and Orange 27%, with the transaction subject to regulatory clearance and expected to close in the second half of 2027.

title: AMD Plans £2B UK AI Investment Over Five Years
summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su announced at London Tech Week that AMD will commit up to £2 billion over five years to accelerate AI innovation in the United Kingdom, covering advanced computing infrastructure, scientific research, and workforce development. The investment includes partnerships with Imperial College London and the University of Cambridge's Zenith AI supercomputer, as well as support for the Sunrise nuclear fusion AI research system.

title: Apple Unveils Major Siri AI Upgrade at WWDC 2026
summary: Apple unveiled a major overhaul of Siri at WWDC 2026 under the branding "Siri AI," introducing a conversational mode with personal context that draws on data from Messages, Mail, Photos, and Calendar. The upgraded assistant gains on-screen awareness, cross-app action capabilities, and conversational continuity, with public availability expected in the fall alongside iOS 27; AI processing is powered in part by Gemini under a reported multi-year deal.

title: Quebec Just Found Out What Not Having Digital Sovereignty Really Means
summary: Columnist Martin Patriquin argues in The Logic that Quebec's $1.5 billion dependency on US-based digital health systems has left the province exposed to the commercial and political priorities of American technology vendors. The piece contends that Canada's broader lack of sovereign digital infrastructure is a structural vulnerability with direct consequences for public services, using Quebec's healthcare systems as a concrete case study.

title: Meta Launches $115 Million 'Workforce Academy' to Train Data Center Workers
summary: Meta announced a $115 million program called America's Workforce Academy, offering free five-week skilled trades training with guaranteed employment at Meta data center sites upon graduation. The program launches in Louisiana, Ohio, Indiana, and Texas, covering roles such as electrical work, HVAC, welding, and fibre-optic technology, developed in partnership with CBRE and the Associated Builders and Contractors. Graduates receive an industry-recognized NCCER credential along with scholarships, housing, and living stipends during the program.

title: OpenAI Confidentially Files IPO Paperwork, Plans Separate Employee Share Sale
summary: OpenAI announced it has filed draft IPO paperwork with the SEC, following rival Anthropic's similar filing a week earlier, though the company said it has not decided on timing and that 'it may be a while' before it goes public. The company plans a separate tender offer allowing employees to sell shares at OpenAI's March 2026 valuation of $852 billion, though employees have not yet been told how much they can sell or when the offer will take place. CEO Sam Altman described this as the start of AI's 'third phase,' in which the central challenge shifts from frontier research to making AI tools abundant and affordable for all.

title: Apple Tries for Another Siri Reboot at WWDC 2026
summary: Apple launched a new version of Siri at its annual developer conference, now called Siri AI and built on Google's Gemini models, featuring a dedicated app and the ability to review past conversations. Demonstrations showed relatively modest capabilities — looking up concert dates, setting reminders, playing songs — without the more autonomous, multi-step actions offered by rival chatbots from OpenAI and Anthropic; several seconds of latency were visible during the keynote. Apple's shares fell 4% following the announcement, and the most advanced on-device AI features will require iPhone 17 Pro or later, effectively requiring a hardware upgrade for full access.

title: U.S. Pentagon Adds Alibaba, Baidu, BYD and Others to Chinese Military Companies Blacklist
summary: The U.S. Department of Defense added more than two dozen Chinese tech companies — including Alibaba, Baidu, BYD, NIO, and memory chip makers YMTC and CXMT — to its list of firms deemed to be acting on behalf of or controlled by the Chinese military. The designation blocks those listed from doing business with the DoD and carries reputational consequences, though it does not prevent U.S. investors from trading their stocks on exchanges. Alibaba, Baidu, and NIO all disputed the move and indicated they would pursue legal action to be removed, while Beijing called the list discriminatory.

title: Bending Spoons Files to Go Public in the U.S.
summary: Italian conglomerate Bending Spoons, which has acquired a string of aging American internet businesses including AOL, Vimeo, and Eventbrite, filed IPO paperwork in the U.S. to raise capital for further acquisitions. The company's revenue doubled to $1.3 billion in 2025 and doubled again in Q1 2026 to $601 million, reflecting its acquisition pace, while operating profit turned positive at $120 million in Q1 compared to a $4.6 million loss in the prior year period. AOL alone generated $333.6 million in operating profits on $633 million of revenue in 2025, validating Bending Spoons' $1.45 billion acquisition price for the legacy internet brand.

title: Databricks in Talks to Raise New Round at Above $165 Billion Valuation
summary: Databricks has held discussions with investors about a new funding round that could launch within the next month, with a target valuation of between $165 billion and $175 billion, according to people with direct knowledge of the conversations. The round would represent a significant jump from the $134 billion valuation set during its late 2025 fundraise, continuing a pattern of repeated private capital raises the 13-year-old company has used to delay going public. Final terms have not been set and it is unclear whether the new valuation would include the fresh funding in the calculation.

title: Anthropic Releases New 'Mythos-Class' Model to General Public With Guardrails
summary: Anthropic released its new Mythos-class AI model to the general public, a release that comes alongside a notable safety guardrail: queries touching on dangerous topics such as cybersecurity or bioweapons will be redirected to an older Opus model rather than the new system. The release marks Anthropic's push to broaden consumer access to its most capable models while maintaining constraints on high-risk use cases. The move comes as Anthropic, like OpenAI, has recently filed confidential IPO paperwork with the SEC.

title: Federal Judge Strikes Down Trump Administration's $100,000 H-1B Visa Fee
summary: A federal judge in Boston invalidated the Trump administration's $100,000 application fee for H-1B visa petitions, ruling that officials exceeded their authority when introducing the charge last fall through executive action. U.S. District Judge Leo Sorokin sided with 20 Democratic state attorneys general who argued the fee functioned as an unauthorized tax and that only Congress holds the power to impose such charges on immigration petitions. The ruling restores the H-1B program to its pre-proclamation cost structure and is expected to be appealed by the White House.

title: Samsung Group Unveils Sweeping AI-Driven Business Overhaul
summary: Samsung Group announced plans for a company-wide AI transformation applying AI across eight core business processes — from procurement and manufacturing to marketing and logistics — framed internally as 'AX,' for AI Transformation. All 50 CEOs of Samsung affiliates will attend an intensive 'AX Bootcamp' executive training program this month, and the company plans to formally deploy external generative AI tools including Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude across all affiliate companies in June. Samsung Electronics separately has set a target to transition all manufacturing into AI-driven factories by 2030.

title: AT&T Scales Cloud RAN as Open RAN Network Swap Surpasses 50%
summary: AT&T completed a controlled introduction phase of its cloud RAN deployment with roughly 25 sites running live traffic on Intel's Sapphire Rapids processors, and is now moving to aggressively scale the implementation. The operator's open RAN replacement of legacy equipment has passed the 50% threshold, making it one of the most advanced large-scale open RAN transitions underway in North America. AT&T's progress serves as a reference point for the broader industry's shift toward software-defined, cloud-native mobile infrastructure.

title: BT Becomes First UK Company to Join Anthropic's Project Glasswing
summary: BT announced it is the first UK-based company to join Anthropic's Project Glasswing, a cybersecurity initiative that uses Anthropic's AI models to strengthen network defenses and improve threat detection. The partnership is aimed at protecting BT's networks against AI-enhanced threats and extending those protections to BT's enterprise customers. The move signals growing interest from major European telecoms in using frontier AI for active cybersecurity rather than passive monitoring.

title: Google Places Order With Intel for Over 3 Million Specialised AI Chips Targeting 2028 Delivery
summary: Alphabet's Google has reportedly placed an order with Intel to manufacture more than 3 million of its specialised AI chips for delivery in 2028, a move that would meaningfully increase pressure on TSMC's dominance in advanced chip manufacturing. The order reflects Google's long-running effort to reduce dependence on a single semiconductor supplier and diversify its AI chip production base beyond custom TPUs made at TSMC. The volume — if confirmed — would rank among the largest single orders Intel has received for AI-specific semiconductor production.

title: UK Government Issues Three-Month Child Safety Ultimatum to Big Tech
summary: The UK government gave major technology companies three months to activate device-level tools that block children from taking, sending, or viewing nude images, warning that regulatory action will follow if they fail to comply. The deadline is part of a broader push to hold platforms accountable for child safety features in operating systems and applications, rather than relying on self-regulation. The ultimatum applies across the major platform operators and comes as regulators in multiple jurisdictions are increasing pressure on tech firms over digital safety for minors.

title: Apple Releases iOS 27 With Speed Improvements and Walks Back Liquid Glass Design
summary: Apple's iOS 27, announced at WWDC, extends software support back to the iPhone 11 and introduces performance gains including app launches up to 30% faster, photo loading 70% faster after capture, and AirDrop transfers 80% faster. The update also adds a transparency slider that lets users dial down the Liquid Glass aesthetic introduced last year, which had generated significant user backlash — an unusually quick design concession for Apple. The software update also opens iCloud Shared Albums to Android and Windows users and adds perimenopause tracking to the Health app.

title: Anthropic and OpenAI Drive Brisk Pace of VC Fund Formation
summary: Venture capital firms are raising new funds at a faster pace than ever before, driven by the need to participate in record-setting funding rounds for AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, according to reporting by The Information. The dynamic reflects how mega-rounds at frontier AI labs — often in the tens of billions of dollars — are forcing VC managers to accelerate their own fundraising cycles to remain competitive investors in the sector. The trend is reshaping fund sizes, timelines, and the competitive dynamics among top-tier venture firms.

title: Sam Altman's Iris-Scanning Startup Tools for Humanity Cuts Staff Amid Revenue Struggles
summary: Tools for Humanity, the company behind Sam Altman's Worldcoin iris-scanning Orb project, is cutting staff after failing to convert its biometrics-for-crypto pitch into meaningful revenue, according to Business Insider. The startup carries a $2.5 billion valuation backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Bain Capital, and Khosla Ventures, but has faced regulatory bans, fines, and privacy probes in multiple countries including South Korea for its practice of paying people around $50 in crypto to scan their eyes. The layoffs come at the same moment OpenAI — Altman's primary company — is moving toward a landmark IPO.

title: Google Agrees to Pay SpaceX $920 Million Per Month for AI Compute Capacity
summary: Google has agreed to pay SpaceX approximately $920 million per month for access to roughly 110,000 Nvidia GPU-powered compute units hosted in SpaceX data centers, according to CNBC. The deal gives Google significant additional GPU capacity at a time when demand for AI infrastructure is outpacing available supply, and signals that non-traditional hyperscalers are becoming relevant compute providers for the largest technology companies. The arrangement expands SpaceX's role beyond launch and satellite operations into AI infrastructure, leveraging its growing data center footprint.

title: Official Advised PM Carney That Banks Must Take Bigger Risks to Diversify Canada's Trade
summary: A government official advised Prime Minister Mark Carney that Canadian banks need to take on greater risk exposure to help firms expand into non-U.S. markets, according to a memo obtained by The Logic covering Carney's meeting with CIBC chief executive Harry Culham. Helping companies make the leap into new international markets was described as a central theme of the meeting, suggesting the federal government is actively pushing major banks to underwrite trade diversification as a policy priority. The memo reveals the behind-the-scenes discussions shaping Canada's post-U.S. trade strategy.

title: Orange Completes Buyout of MasOrange Spanish Joint Venture
summary: Orange completed the acquisition of its partner's stake in MasOrange, the Spanish joint venture the company had operated alongside another telecom operator, consolidating full control of the business. The move follows another acquisition by Orange in the preceding days and signals a broader push to consolidate its Southern European footprint ahead of potential market restructuring. MasOrange is one of Spain's largest mobile operators, making the full buyout a significant step in Orange's Iberian strategy.
